input_basis: Only the required brief.md was used for initial discovery; the exact plan remained unreleased at capture time.
source_access_timestamp_method: The browser tool does not expose an exact per-page retrieval second. accessed_utc is the UTC clock sampled immediately after the final verification batch completed; pages were first surfaced during the 04:19-04:24 UTC research window. Search-result-only or JavaScript-limited sources state that limitation in observed_operation.

sources.title: Extension Host | Visual Studio Code Extension API
sources.version_or_commit: Current unversioned documentation; no release or commit is declared on the page.
sources.locator: Sections Extension Host configurations and Extension Host runtimes (search-result excerpt; direct page fetch timed out).
sources.observed_operation: Official page located by web search; excerpt read, direct open retried and timed out. No source code or tests executed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Lists local Node, web Worker, and remote Node extension hosts depending on configuration/capabilities/location. It describes placement and runtime, not data permissions.
sources.applicability: Supports process/runtime alternatives and the caution that host placement is not an authorization promise.

sources.title: Workspace Trust
sources.version_or_commit: Current VS Code documentation retrieved 2026-10-12; no release or commit is declared on the page.
sources.locator: Restricted Mode; caution that Workspace Trust cannot prevent a malicious extension from executing code that ignores it.
sources.observed_operation: Official page opened and relevant sections read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Restricted Mode disables or limits features and extensions, but the page explicitly says it cannot prevent malicious extensions from executing code and ignoring Restricted Mode.
sources.applicability: A trust prompt or extension opt-in is insufficient as the boundary for access to unrelated notes.

sources.title: Custom Editor API
sources.version_or_commit: Current unversioned VS Code API documentation; no release or commit is declared.
sources.locator: Custom Editor API basics, readonly editor providers, lifecycle, invalid structured documents, multiple webview/document models.
sources.observed_operation: Official documentation opened and relevant sections read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Custom editor view is a webview; extension provides the document model. Read-only previews have less save/backing responsibility. Invalid structured documents should be handled or reported to user.
sources.applicability: Useful interface/lifecycle precedent for third-party previews, while not itself proving a security sandbox.

sources.title: Webview API
sources.version_or_commit: Current unversioned VS Code API documentation; no release or commit is declared.
sources.locator: Security: Limit capabilities, Content security policy, Only load content over https, Sanitize all user input.
sources.observed_operation: Official page search excerpt and opened page inspected; security section lines 924-980 in captured result.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Scripts should be off when unnecessary; localResourceRoots may be empty; CSP is restrictive by example; input sanitization is required but not sufficient alone.
sources.applicability: Guides renderer hardening and shows why extension markup cannot be trusted or granted host bridge access.

sources.title: Process Model | Electron
sources.version_or_commit: Latest unversioned Electron docs retrieved 2026-10-12; page does not pin a release.
sources.locator: The Utility Process section (search-result excerpt; direct open timed out).
sources.observed_operation: Official page located by web search; excerpt read, direct open retried and timed out.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: UtilityProcess can isolate untrusted, CPU-intensive, or crash-prone services from main; it runs Node and exposes Node APIs. This does not by itself show a notebook-specific permission policy.
sources.applicability: Shows process separation can help responsiveness while a separate authority model remains necessary.

sources.title: utilityProcess API | Electron
sources.version_or_commit: Latest unversioned Electron docs retrieved 2026-10-12; no release number on page.
sources.locator: utilityProcess.fork options; child.kill; exit events; default env/session and macOS flags.
sources.observed_operation: Official API page opened; utility process capabilities and lifecycle inspected.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Child runs Node with message ports; env defaults to process.env, stdio to inherit; macOS unsigned-library flag defaults false; kill is graceful SIGTERM on POSIX.
sources.applicability: Useful worker/supervision reference. Strip ambient env, do not inherit unnecessary resources, and don't interpret the API as sandboxing by itself.

sources.title: Process Sandboxing | Electron
sources.version_or_commit: Electron docs state renderer sandbox enabled by default since Electron 20; latest unversioned page retrieved 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Sandbox behavior, renderer IPC, Node integration exception, untrusted-content caveat, release update responsibilities.
sources.observed_operation: Official page opened and security/configuration sections read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Sandbox is enabled for renderers by default from Electron 20. nodeIntegration:true or sandbox:false disables it; privileged operations go through IPC. Electron states app vendors must ship underlying security updates.
sources.applicability: Useful embedded-renderer precedent; configure exact version/defaults and minimize IPC bridge, not a direct extension host choice.

sources.title: Wasmtime Security
sources.version_or_commit: main branch, unpinned; source is mutable and should be tied to the chosen release commit before implementation.
sources.locator: WebAssembly Core, Filesystem Access, and Terminal Output sections.
sources.observed_operation: Official project source documentation opened; security-model section read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WebAssembly must explicitly import host functionality; WASI filesystem capabilities constrain paths to granted directories. The page also warns about control sequences in untrusted terminal output.
sources.applicability: Useful rationale for capability-limited execution and careful output handling; advisory history demonstrates residual implementation risk.

sources.title: WASI Tutorial | Wasmtime
sources.version_or_commit: main branch, unpinned; tutorial examples may age and must be checked against selected release.
sources.locator: Preopened directories, --dir, path traversal and symlink discussion.
sources.observed_operation: Official tutorial search excerpt inspected.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A WASI guest gets filesystem capabilities only for preopened directories; example demonstrates denied access outside them. Later advisory history documents a bug in this implementation path.
sources.applicability: Supports an attachment-only capability prototype, but must not be treated as proof that runtime path confinement is bug-free.

sources.title: Config in wasmtime - Rust
sources.version_or_commit: Latest unversioned API docs; versioned use not established by this page.
sources.locator: consume_fuel, epoch_interruption, instrumentation cost and determinism.
sources.observed_operation: Official API docs opened and fuel/epoch sections read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Fuel counts guest instructions with overhead and gives precise accounting; epoch checks are cheaper but non-deterministic/coarse and need engine epoch increments.
sources.applicability: Indicates guest CPU controls are runtime-configured options, not sufficient controls for host calls, wall time, or other resource use.

sources.title: Store in wasmtime - Rust
sources.version_or_commit: docs.rs latest endpoint as served 2026-10-12; pin a semver release and commit for implementation.
sources.locator: ResourceLimiterAsync behavior; set_epoch_deadline and epoch_deadline_trap.
sources.observed_operation: Official Rust API reference opened; resource and epoch documentation read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Limiter applies to future resource creation/growth, is not retroactive; async limiter requires async APIs. Epoch deadline defaults to immediately elapsed and must be set for a future deadline.
sources.applicability: Supports explicit memory/table limiter configuration and tests for all execution paths.

sources.title: Filesystem sandbox escape when paths or symlinks contain trailing slashes
sources.version_or_commit: Advisory GHSA-vqjp-4c8c-hfgg, published 2026-08-20; patch versions 24.0.13, 36.0.14, 46.0.3, 47.0.4; 48.0.0+ reported unaffected.
sources.locator: Affected/patched versions, impact, Linux openat2 condition, patch/workaround.
sources.observed_operation: Official GitHub security advisory opened; affected versions and impact read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Trailing slash/symlink paths could escape WASI filesystem sandbox on affected releases; specific issue not present with Linux kernel >5.6 using openat2, while macOS/older Linux are affected.
sources.applicability: Requires patch/version monitoring and symlink/trailing-slash cross-platform regression tests; do not infer that capability APIs eliminate path bugs.

sources.title: Guest-controlled resource exhaustion in WASI implementations
sources.version_or_commit: Advisory published 2026-02-24; patch releases include 24.0.6, 36.0.6, 40.0.4, 41.0.4, 42.0.0.
sources.locator: Impact; WASIp1/WASIp2; host memory, handles, I/O buffers; default limit behavior by release.
sources.observed_operation: Official advisory opened; affected versions, host API pathways, patch caveat read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Guest-controlled host allocations/buffering could exhaust memory or crash; older patched stable branches kept limits very large by default; 42.0.0+ defaults were tuned to avoid the reported issue.
sources.applicability: Bound host-call data, buffers, handles, output, and disk separately; runtime patch alone may not select safe embedder quotas.

sources.title: WASI preview 0 poll_oneoff circumvents fuel consumption
sources.version_or_commit: Advisory published 2026-10-02; referenced by Wasmtime v49.0.2 release.
sources.locator: Advisory title and v49.0.2 release fix list; advisory body was not fully parsed by browser.
sources.observed_operation: Official release and advisory index search results read; linked advisory body open returned no parsed lines.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WASI poll_oneoff could circumvent guest fuel consumption; Wasmtime v49.0.2 lists the fix.
sources.applicability: Fuel alone is not proof of bounded execution through every imported/host path; add an external wall-clock watchdog and regression coverage.

sources.title: Wasmtime Releases: v49.0.2
sources.version_or_commit: v49.0.2 released 2026-10-02; verified commit prefix 3c8a3e7.
sources.locator: Release 49.0.2 and linked fixes, especially GHSA-j366-h8gg-77pm and GHSA-gqmc-89g8-p25r.
sources.observed_operation: Official release page opened and release fixes reviewed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Release includes security fixes; later patch releases may supersede it. Do not assume current advisories remain exhausted.
sources.applicability: Use as a concrete pin/history example only; any implementation should select and continuously update a reviewed, supported release.

sources.title: Testing | Wasmtime
sources.version_or_commit: Latest unversioned Wasmtime contributor docs retrieved 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Running WASI Integration Tests and Adding WASI Integration Tests; crates/test-programs and cargo test -p wasmtime-wasi.
sources.observed_operation: Official test guide opened and relevant commands/paths read; tests were not run.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WASI integration test command compiles test programs; guide names crates/test-programs and crates/wasi/tests/all/preview1.rs plus preview2 integration paths.
sources.applicability: Potential upstream regression-test starting point if Wasmtime is selected; not evidence that product-specific extension behavior is covered.

sources.title: SQLite FTS5 Extension
sources.version_or_commit: Current SQLite documentation accessed 2026-10-12; contentless-delete feature noted as available since SQLite 3.43.0.
sources.locator: External Content and Contentless Tables; external content pitfalls; synchronization triggers and integrity-check.
sources.observed_operation: Official SQLite reference opened; source-table synchronization requirements read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: External-content FTS rows must be kept synchronized by the application; stale index/content mismatch yields unintuitive results. Triggers do not backfill existing rows.
sources.applicability: Use separate preview artifact/source-type rows and transactional index synchronization; test rebuild and provenance joins.

sources.title: SQLite Transaction
sources.version_or_commit: Current SQLite documentation accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Transactions, read versus write, default DEFERRED behavior, and busy commit conditions.
sources.observed_operation: Official SQLite page opened and transaction semantics read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: SQLite permits multiple readers but only one simultaneous writer; commit can return SQLITE_BUSY. A single transaction groups DB changes.
sources.applicability: Coordinate run-state and search-index changes in transactions while handling busy/retry behavior; database atomicity does not make filesystem deletion safe.

sources.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
sources.version_or_commit: Current SQLite documentation accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Introduction and rollback-journal atomic commit scope.
sources.observed_operation: Official SQLite technical note opened.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Explains atomic transaction property for a single database file, specifically rollback-journal mode; WAL has separate documentation.
sources.applicability: Database metadata transitions may be transactional, but an artifact file and the DB row need a deliberate publish/reconcile protocol.

sources.title: Accessing files from the macOS App Sandbox
sources.version_or_commit: Current Apple developer documentation accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Overview; security-scoped URL lifetime and startAccessingSecurityScopedResource / stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource.
sources.observed_operation: Official documentation search excerpt read; page open exposes JavaScript limitation but provided Markdown excerpt.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: User-selected URLs extend app access; security-scoped access must be started and stopped; file ACL/MAC controls may still deny.
sources.applicability: A broad notebook folder grant is too broad for one attachment; avoid passing reusable security-scoped roots into an extension.

sources.title: Process | Foundation
sources.version_or_commit: Current Apple Foundation documentation accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Sandbox note on child processes and XPC alternatives.
sources.observed_operation: Official search excerpt read; page open requires JavaScript.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A child launched by Process inside a sandboxed app inherits the parent's sandbox; different helper entitlements require XPC services.
sources.applicability: A plain spawned child is not a per-extension permission sandbox on macOS.

sources.title: XPC | Apple Developer Documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current Apple XPC documentation accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Overview and service type table; privilege isolation, process lifetime, on-demand launch/restart.
sources.observed_operation: Official Apple developer search excerpt read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: XPC services are separate processes; an XPC service per client is tied to the client lifetime. Different service types carry different user/root context.
sources.applicability: Potential macOS containment implementation; configure minimal service entitlements and narrow IPC rather than passing notebook access.

sources.title: AppContainer isolation - Win32 apps
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Learn documentation; AppContainer feature introduced in Windows 8.
sources.locator: File, network, process isolation; capability grants.
sources.observed_operation: Official Microsoft Learn search result inspected.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Resources are isolated by default with specific capabilities granted as needed; user/application identities and ACLs also govern access.
sources.applicability: Candidate Windows sandbox primitive; validate packaged/unpackaged launch support and each requested capability on supported Windows versions.

sources.title: Job Objects - Win32 apps
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Learn documentation retrieved 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Managing processes in jobs, job limits, process-tree limitations and breakaway flags.
sources.observed_operation: Official page opened; process inheritance, limits, and tree management sections read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Children created with CreateProcess join by default, but breakaway flags/settings and some process creation paths bypass the job. Nested jobs require Windows 8+.
sources.applicability: Use for process-tree CPU/memory/time/termination only with breakaway disabled or explicitly handled and tested.

sources.title: Control Group v2 — Linux Kernel documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Linux kernel v6.6 documentation.
sources.locator: Memory and CPU controllers, including memory.max and cpu.max.
sources.observed_operation: Official kernel documentation search result read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Cgroup controls account/limit process-group resource use; kernel documents possible over/under reclaim around memory targets.
sources.applicability: Candidate Linux resource limits for whole worker tree; requires cgroup delegation/permissions and runtime support checks.

sources.title: seccomp(2) — Linux manual page
sources.version_or_commit: Current Linux man-pages documentation retrieved 2026-10-12; kernel feature details are version-conditioned in the page.
sources.locator: Filter actions, thread synchronization flags, SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS.
sources.observed_operation: Linux man page search excerpt read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Filters constrain system calls; available flags/actions vary by kernel version and filters do not by themselves define filesystem/network namespace or CPU/memory budgets.
sources.applicability: One part of Linux defense-in-depth; feature-probe at runtime and pair with resource and filesystem controls.
